## ===== pack-r1.md (this pack) =====

# Gate 50 · the GSW 6a fills gate: #366 (with LE-g50) and #368 · round 1

Round 1. The auditor is Codex, under the standing ruling of 2026-11-11 (Codex for audits and reviews). This is **Gate 50**,
the fills gate of GSW phase 6a: the proofs of the 98 6a targets that Gate 45 froze as statements. Seyoon's ruling of
2026-11-17 (decision-log line 578, "#368 gating (Seyoon): fold into Gate 50") audits the 6b owner prerequisites #368 here as
well. Two open draft PRs are audited:

- **PR #366** ([link](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/pull/366)), branch `land/gsw-6a-fills`, head
  **`597fb736e545706a058cc212243a13f6dadfeceb`** (tree `df05652d512a702fa8e379fe3f16258f0e1d20d5`), base
  `cryptography/pass-shelat-ch2-4`. Its merge base with the records tip and its REST `base.sha` are both
  `555f0fe1b10a20d1be72386a97c6fe7a2f39c204`. It has 22 SSH-signed first-parent commits since the branch point
  `036d823933c8248bd8894c7963e15dd0f1837075` (`checks/series.txt`). It changes 24 files (+6435/−214) against its merge
  base.
- **PR #368** ([link](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/pull/368)), branch `land/gsw-6b-owner-prereqs`, head
  **`1953898b18a33ab2cd533820c5754a1aacffeb44`** (tree `89952a4a153c1183e0345f88a10568a936762a7d`), one SSH-signed commit on
  `55f553715f280be36827ad86a94c93db39ec56c3` (its REST `base.sha` and merge base). 2 files, +33/−12.
- **Records pin:** the commit that files this directory, `briefs/lattice-gsw/gates/50-gsw-6a-fills/`. `dispatch-r1.md`
  and the prompt name it. Its parent is the records tip at staging, `f19b8056488fb01214d00915064669dda7e65cc2`
  ("Records: LE-g50 on #366 (PASS; TreeNCAC seal failures cleared)"), and the pin adds only this directory, so every
  record this pack cites reads the same at `f19b8056` and at the pin.

## Questions for the audit

**1. Correctness of the proofs (all 98 targets, and every helper)**
- Does every proof establish its Gate-45-frozen statement? The axiom probe (phase 2; LE-g50 re-run) reports all 98
  targets on `propext`/`Classical.choice`/`Quot.sound` only, 0 `sorryAx`, 0 TRACE lines over the 853-constant census.
  Spot-check the hard units for hidden weakenings (a target proved for a special case through an instance argument, a
  `decide`/kernel case check that does not cover the statement):
  - U3: C10's explicit conjugator (`conjugator_conj`, by orbit matching and `IsFiveCycle.pow_apply_eq_iff`), C13's
    commutator and De Morgan steps, C14's `4 ^ depth` bound, `isFiveCycle_commutator` by `decide +kernel`.
  - U4 (Thm 2, C17–C21) and U5 (NC¹ corollaries C22–C25).
  - U7 (N7–N13: the layering; `NANDLayering`'s structural and semantic column invariants).
  - U9–U11 (carry-save, comparison, modular interval sum: F5–F10).
  - U6 (N1–N6: the NAND gadget through `DAGCircuit.rewrite`).
- Are the 57 private helpers true as stated and used as their docstrings say?
- #368: is `decrypt_eq_decode_dotProduct` true for every `P`, `s`, `C` (the `Fin.snoc` split at the last coordinate,
  `secretVector_eq`), and does `decrypt_eq_decode_errorSum` still prove its unchanged statement? Is `hybridPlant_eq` the
  definition's body verbatim?

## Findings delivery

Return `gate50-gsw-6a-fills-findings.md` as Markdown in this chat. If you have several evidence files, return a ZIP. The
user dispatches and merges.

| # | Severity | PR · file · declaration | Claim | Evidence | Proposed fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Number the findings **G50-01, G50-02, …**. Grade GF-F01 to GF-F09 and U1–U3 in a separate table. Report the audited
heads, the records pin, the counts by severity, and a verdict **per PR** (#366, #368) and **overall**:
- **CLEAR:** zero blockers and zero majors.
- **HOLD:** otherwise.

**Severities**
- **blocker:** a false or unusable statement, a proof that does not establish its statement, or a scope violation.
- **major:** any of the following:
  - a changed frozen statement or statement prose (other than the ruled LE-gf2 exception and permitted sketch updates);
  - a forbidden read not covered by the rulings;
  - an undisclosed copied private lemma, or an undisclosed (or unaccepted) re-proof of a public one;
  - a fabricated source tag;
  - necessary evidence that cannot be verified or does not bind to the audited commit.
- **minor:** documentation or API defects, including an inaccurate formula docstring, glue note, proof sketch, citation
  or PR description.
- **note:** anything else.

  C23. This is the G48-01 pattern. It is closed by the landing edit LE-gf1 (a 2-line reuse).

  copies, and 12 of the 16 are byte-identical within their family. This is the worker's GF-W1.
  Under policy §1 and G44-01 it needs Seyoon's acceptance or repayment.

    (a #360 addendum, like `cc05f76c`), and two `CarrySave` helpers are made public.
  - The alternative is a ledger row, DL-61.

There are two minors (GF-F03, GF-F04) and five infos.

  patches reproduce `bb7efa82af89141535e7a4adc49c6d97aef85de8` hash for hash, and `src/` is byte-identical.
- **Scope:** only the six files change. Outside proof bodies, sketches and private helpers, the only changes are the
  permitted sentences, the G6A-F07 line and four Mathlib imports. decls2 gives 0/0/0.
- **Admissions:** 74 in 12 modules, none in the owned files.

- **D1. Three readers are not `rfl` (census said `rfl`).** `TreeCircuit.depth`, `size` and `maxFanin` are defined by
  well-founded recursion, so they are `@[irreducible]`.
  - A probe on the snapshot showed `rfl` failing on all three (`#print` shows `⋯.fix`; log in `probe/`).
  - They are proved by `simp [TreeCircuit.depth]` (and likewise for `size` and `maxFanin`), through the definitions'
    own equation lemmas `depth.eq_1` and so on. The owner unfolds its own definition, which is the form of the sibling
    reader `TreeCircuit.eval_lit`.
  - All three use the standard axioms, as `depth_node` does. The PR title keeps "pure rfl insertions" as given; the
    body discloses this deviation.
- **D2. Docstrings over two lines.** Five docstrings (`carryBit_succ`, `gatesAcyclic_iff`, `isWellFormed_iff`,
  `isPolySize_iff`, `hasPolylogDepth_iff`) take two lines, and `gadgetCorrect_iff` and `inTreeNC_iff` take three. The
  reason is that the formula and "Glue." do not fit in 100 columns. No added line is longer than 100 characters.
- **D3. First commit attempt.** The first signed commit, `faef08bd…` (never pushed), wrote `carryBit_succ` as

```diff
+
 /-- The depth of vertex `v` after running `gs` over `n` inputs. -/
 def vertexDepth (n : ℕ) (gs : List DAGGate) (v : ℕ) : ℕ :=
   (runWith DAGGate.depth gs (List.replicate n 0)).getD v 0
 
+/-- Reader of `vertexDepth`:
+`vertexDepth n gs v = (runWith DAGGate.depth gs (List.replicate n 0)).getD v 0`.  Glue. -/
+theorem vertexDepth_eq (n : ℕ) (gs : List DAGGate) (v : ℕ) :
+    vertexDepth n gs v = (runWith DAGGate.depth gs (List.replicate n 0)).getD v 0 := rfl
+
```

## ===== briefs/lattice-gsw/phase6/rulings.md (records, at b1392d065d0a8f496db8e01b6bdad746bc847ffe) =====

# GSW phase 6 · rulings P6-Q1 to P6-Q13 and the location ruling (Seyoon, 2026-11-16)

Seyoon answered the thirteen questions in [questions.md](questions.md): eight as recommended and five changed (Q3, Q4,
Q9, Q10, Q11). He then added a location ruling. `plan-section.md` is revised to match before the statement phase.

| # | Ruling | |
|---|---|---|
| P6-Q1 | **One phase 6** on the BV14 route to pure FHE at a polynomial ratio; it merges the roadmap's phases 6 and 7. **Two statement gates:** **Gate 45** covers the complexity layer (6a: branching programs, Barrington, formula arithmetic, NAND conversion), and **Gate 46** covers the cryptography (6b). The quasi-polynomial instantiation is dropped. Gates 42–44 are taken, so 45 and 46 replace the plan's provisional 42 and 43. | as recommended |
| P6-Q2 | Barrington's input model is **`BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit n`**, AND/OR formulas over literals with polarity, which is Bar89's model. `DAGCircuit` is reached through the depth-preserving `DAGCircuit.toTree`. | as recommended |
| P6-Q3 | **Both directions now: BWBP = NC¹.** This covers Bar89 Thm 1 with Lemmas 1–3, the `DAGCircuit` corollary (length ≤ `4^depth`), NC¹ ⊆ polynomial-length width-5 PBPs, **and** Thm 2 (BWBP ⊆ NC¹) with its composition-tree circuit. The plan's estimate is about +300–500 lines; FHE does not use Thm 2. | **changed** (was: Thm 1 and NC¹ ⊆ PBP only) |
| P6-Q4 | **The general branching-program model of Bar89 §1**, with instructions mapping `[w] → [w]`, plus an **`IsPermutation`** predicate. It is otherwise as proposed: instructions `⟨var, f0, f1⟩` in BV14's order (`f0` when the bit is `0`), with Bar89's order disclosed; `yield` in program order; and the public host `evalWith`, generic in the selector and value type, with the step-indexed relational lemma `evalWith_rel`. It is registered in `ComputationalModels.lean` and `machine-library-design.md` §14. Boolean semantics and GSW are its consumers. | **changed** (was: permutation programs only) |
| P6-Q5 | The decryption formula is built in a **new shared formula-arithmetic layer** over `TreeCircuit`: De Morgan negation, substitution, `xor3`/`maj3`, the carry-save (3:2) reduction, carry-out comparison with constants, and the modular interval sum. | as recommended |
| P6-Q6 | The layer goes in **`Complexity/CircuitComplexity/FormulaArith/{Combinators,CarrySave,Compare,ModSum}.lean`**, as the first rows of a circuit/formula gadget registry. A small owner-side PR promotes the private `TreeNCAC.combine` to public. `Parity.lean`'s private dual-rail XOR is re-pointed later, on the dedup queue. At statement prep, check `Complexity/FormulaKit/Gate.lean` (CNF truth-table gates) for reuse; it is a different formula model. | as recommended |
| P6-Q7 | **`decode_iff_mem_Ico`**, with explicit `lo` and `hi`, is a published reader in the owner file `LWE/BitEncoding.lean`, added by a small owner-side PR. | as recommended |
| P6-Q8 | The evaluation key is **public-key GSW encryptions, under the user's own `pk`, of the `N` bits of `G⁻¹(t)` with `t = (−s, 1)`**. This is BV11 Def 3.8. There is one `GSW.Parameters` record, the evaluation-key noise is `m·B`, and decryption becomes a binary subset sum with public constants `Gᵀc`. | as recommended |
| P6-Q9 | **Bootstrapping is NAND only**, literally BV14 Def 2.13. Circuits are first converted to NAND form by a **new conversion with its own lemmas** (semantics, size and depth). | **changed** (was: every `DAGCircuit` gate) |
| P6-Q10 | **The concrete statements, and now also the asymptotic forms:** an asymptotic `WeakCircularSecure` family predicate and an asymptotic IND-CPA theorem, conditional on an explicit reduction-efficiency hypothesis. Concrete as in phase 5: `WeakCircularSecure P χ ε` bounds every distinguisher's advantage on `(pk, evk, Enc(μ))`, and the `evk`-free view inherits phase 5's DLWE bound. Compactness holds by typing and is stated in the docstring. | **changed** (was: concrete only, asymptotic later) |
| P6-Q11 | **The full leveled scheme now:** `L+1` keys, correctness, and IND-CPA by a hybrid over the keys from DLWE (BV14 Thm 2.14 first part; BV11 Thm 3.1). The plan's estimate is about +400–700 lines. It is the FHE statement that needs no circular-security assumption. The key-switching form of the bootstrapping lemma remains its basis. | **changed** (was: key-switching lemma only) |
| P6-Q12 | **Explicit `decDepth P` and `bootNoise P β`** in the correctness theorems, with closed-form bounds proved separately. The ruled `RatioBounded F B p` goes in a new `LWE/Ratio.lean`, with a family theorem carrying an explicit `PolyExpr` `pBoot`. | as recommended |
| P6-Q13 | **`barrington` is computable**: Lemma 1's conjugator is explicit (`θ(σᵏ 0) = τᵏ 0` for five-cycles), so `fheEval` is computable. | as recommended |

## Location ruling (Seyoon, 2026-11-16, after Q1–Q13)

**Branching programs, Barrington and the NAND conversion go in `Complexity/`.** In Seyoon's words, these are general
facts about models of computation and will be usable elsewhere. The 6b (GSW) modules only consume them.

The maintainer proposes these homes; the revised plan section confirms them:
- **Branching programs.** The facade is `Complexity/BranchingPrograms.lean`, with:
  - `Complexity/BranchingPrograms/Defs.lean`: the general model, `IsPermutation` and `yield`;
  - `Complexity/BranchingPrograms/Eval.lean`: the host `evalWith` and `evalWith_rel`;
  - `Complexity/BranchingPrograms/Barrington.lean`: Thm 1, Lemmas 1–3 and the NC¹ corollary;
  - `Complexity/BranchingPrograms/BarringtonConverse.lean`: Thm 2.

  The model is registered in `ComputationalModels.lean`.
- **NAND conversion:** `Complexity/CircuitComplexity/NANDForm.lean`, beside `DAGTransform.lean`.
- **Formula arithmetic:** `Complexity/CircuitComplexity/FormulaArith/`, per P6-Q6.

## Effect on scope
The changed rulings enlarge the phase:
- Thm 2 adds about 300–500 lines (P6-Q3), and the leveled scheme about 400–700 (P6-Q11), per the plan's estimates.
- The general BP model (P6-Q4), the NAND conversion (P6-Q9) and the asymptotic forms (P6-Q10) are new items. The revised
  plan section estimates them.
- Gate 45 (6a) now covers the BP model, Barrington in both directions, formula arithmetic and the NAND conversion.

## Rulings P6-Q14 to P6-Q19 (Seyoon, 2026-11-16, on plan section r2)

| # | Ruling | |
|---|---|---|
| P6-Q14 | **Consecutive keys plus a layering conversion.** Each `evk_d` encrypts the bits of `s_{d−1}`, giving `N·L` ciphertexts (the textbook chain). Circuits are made **layered** by a new generic conversion under `Complexity/`, which pads uneven paths with double-NAND identity chains, with care for odd gaps. It is part of 6a and Gate 45; estimated +150–250 lines. | **changed** (was: keys by depth, evk to every lower key) |
| P6-Q15 | **Per-distinguisher concrete form:** `WeakCircularSecure P χ D ε := distAdv (fheView … false) (fheView … true) D ≤ ε`. The asymptotic `WeakCircularSecureFamily` (NUPPT, negligible) is the headline hypothesis, faithful to BV11 Def 3.8. This corrects P6-Q10's concrete form, which, quantified over every function, holds only for `ε` near 1. | as recommended |
| P6-Q16 | **NAND form is a predicate on `DAGCircuit`:** every gate is a `¬` gate (negated conjunction) of fan-in ≤ 2. The conversion is an instance of `DAGCircuit.rewrite`, within its budget, with depth factor 2. Bootstrapping pads fan-in 1 to `(a, a)` and fan-in 0 to `(G, G)`. Disclosed: NAND-form circuits are not `IsWellFormed`. | as recommended |
| P6-Q17 | **Registry rows:** `BranchingProgram.evalWith` as H18; `runWith`/`runWith_rel` recorded as H19 and `DAGCircuit.rewrite` as H20. Gate 45 audits their contracts. Records only. | as recommended |
| P6-Q18 | **Thm 2's circuit is a `TreeCircuit` formula** with fan-in 2, mirroring Bar89's three sections. It reaches `DAGCircuit` and `Language.InNC 1` through `Language.InTreeNC.inNC`; its size `l^{O(log w)}` is polynomial for fixed `w`. | as recommended |
| P6-Q19 | **Ingest Gen09:** the leveled-bootstrapping passage of Gentry's thesis or his STOC 2009 paper (the key chain and its security hybrid), which is cited for the leveled scheme. **Needs the PDF from Seyoon.** Until then the 6b leveled-scheme statements wait; 6a is unaffected. | **changed** (was: no new ingest) |

Effect: 6a gains the layering conversion (P6-Q14). 6b's leveled scheme uses the consecutive chain over layered circuits and cites
Gen09 once ingested. The plan section is updated to r3 accordingly.

**P6-Q19, refinement (Seyoon, 2026-11-16, same day):** Gen09 must not be a bottleneck. Seyoon sends the PDF later today, and
it affects only docstrings. Nothing waits for it.
- The 6b leveled statements proceed now, citing only ingested sources ([BV11, Thm 3.1, Def 3.6]; [BV14, Thm 2.14 first
  part, Thm 3.7]; [AP14, §5.3]) and disclosing that the key-chain construction and hybrid order are reconstructed.
- After the ingest, a docstring-only follow-up adds the [Gen09] citation. No Lean docstring cites [Gen09] before then.

## Why

Seyoon ruled **Q-C1** on 2026-11-17 (decision log `LatticeCryptographyPlan.md`). It resolves finding **G6B-C1-F03** of `briefs/lattice-gsw/phase6/checkpoint1-6b-review.md`:

- **The G6 fill needs a lemma that is private.** The fill of `decryptFormula_eval` needs the step `c_last − ⟨s, c_init⟩ = ⟨t, decryptColumn P C⟩`, where `t = (−s, 1)`. That step exists only inside the private `decrypt_eq_decode_errorSum`. A 6b file must not copy private material across files (the GF-F02 pattern).
- **The ruling.** The lemma becomes an owner-side public lemma in `GSW/Scheme.lean`. It lands with the `hybridPlant` reader before the 6b fills.
- **The reader census.** The 6b reader census (`briefs/lattice-gsw/phase6/issued-6b-r1/census.txt`) lists `hybridPlant` as `MISSING`. The statement job adds `decrypt_eq_decode_dotProduct` to the census as MISSING too.

## Changes

There is one signed commit, `1953898b18a33ab2cd533820c5754a1aacffeb44`, on the records tip `55f553715f280be36827ad86a94c93db39ec56c3`. That tip is Lean-equal to the T of snapshot #7, `a1fa7b65`. The diff is +33/−12.

1. **`GSW/Scheme.lean`**
   - New public lemma `decrypt_eq_decode_dotProduct (P) (s) (C) : decrypt P s C = LWE.BitEncoding.decode P.lwe (secretVector P s ⬝ᵥ decryptColumn P C)`.
     - It sits right after `decrypt_eq`.
     - Its docstring states the formula, cites [GSW13, §3.1, `Dec`; BV14, §3.1, `NCCrypt.Dec`] like the file's other docstrings, and has a proof sketch.
     - It is step 1 (`hsplit`) of the private `decrypt_eq_decode_errorSum`, promoted.
   - Only the **proof body** of `decrypt_eq_decode_errorSum` changes: `hsplit` is replaced by `rw [decrypt_eq_decode_dotProduct, decryptColumn_eq]`, and the redundant `rw [decrypt_eq, Regev.decrypt_eq]; dsimp only; rw [hsplit, …]` becomes `rw […]`. Its statement and docstring are unchanged.
2. **`Encryption/PublicKey/EnsembleSecurity.lean`**
   - New definitional reader `hybridPlant_eq … (pc) (r) : hybridPlant E m m' j D pc r = D (pc.1, fun i => if i < j then … else if i = j then pc.2 else …) r.2 := rfl`.
   - It sits beside `hybridPlant` and follows the file's reader style (`pkEncDist_eq`).

The brief gave `PrivateKey/EnsembleSecurity.lean`. `hybridPlant` is actually in `PublicKey/EnsembleSecurity.lean:110`, which is also the path the census gives.

**Search for existing equivalents.** No equivalent of either lemma exists:

- Neither name occurs in `TCSlib/` or `audits/` at the tip, on `land/gsw-6a-fills` (#366, `ccca6f80`), or in the 6b statement delivery (exchange `1e0647b9`, `src/`, `src-o2/` and both patch series). Both files are identical on #366, and the 6b delivery does not touch them.

## ===== verification-r1.zip:POINTERS.md (this pack) =====

# POINTERS · what is not copied

- **The Lean sources** are in `sources-r1.zip` beside this ZIP (heads, the Gate-45 freeze, the merge base, before LE-g50,
  #368 base and head), and in the repository at the pinned commits.
- **The worker's delivery** (`inbox/fills/gsw-6a-fills/` on `exchange/pass-shelat-ch5-8`, final
  `607034428468ffd88adec313eb293e3e60520f59`: REPORT, 7 patches, `src/`, 939 evidence files) is not copied; phase 1
  recounted it and the phase-1 ZIP holds the recount.
- **The issued fills package** is `briefs/lattice-gsw/phase6/issued-fills-r1/` at the records pin; only `brief.md`,
  `targets.txt` and `fill-environment-addendum.md` are copied (`tools/`, `order.txt`, `closures.txt`, `roots.txt` and
  `base-sorries.txt` are not).
- **#360's addendum** (`vertexValue_eq`, `vertexDepth_eq`) has its record in `records/phase6/readers-q3/
  addendum-vertex-readers.md`; its evidence directory (`$SP/fill86/rd/ev/`) was never filed in the records. The
  addendum's downstream is covered by #366's phase-2 replay.
- **The in-house drafts' own build evidence** (`$SP/fill12/`, `$SP/fill86/`) is not filed; their content is covered by
  phase 2, the #7 re-replay and LE-g50.
- **Gate 45's pack and evidence** are `briefs/lattice-gsw/gates/45-gsw-6a/` at the records pin (only the findings and
  resolutions are copied).
- **The olean trees** (`olean-replay-6a-land8`, the #368 replays, the snapshots) are on the maintainer's host only.

    included): empty (`step3-diff.txt`). From #7's T to the merge, the only Lean change is

    `5eaddd17` (`replay-statecheck.out`).

+  by_cases hA : A x
+  · rw [if_pos hA, (h.2 x).1 hA]
+  · rw [if_neg hA, (h.2 x).2 hA, Perm.coe_one]
+
+/-- Five-cycle recognition only depends on the recognized set: if `B` five-cycle recognizes `A`
+with output `σ` and `A x ↔ A' x` for all `x`, then it recognizes `A'`.  Glue for C13. -/
+private theorem FiveCycleRecognizes.of_iff {B : BranchingProgram 5 n}
+    {A A' : (Fin n → Bool) → Prop} {σ : Perm (Fin 5)} (h : FiveCycleRecognizes B A σ)
+    (hA : ∀ x, A x ↔ A' x) : FiveCycleRecognizes B A' σ := by
+  have hAA : A = A' := funext fun x => propext (hA x)
+  subst hAA
+  exact h
+
+/-- **The `∧` step** of [Bar89, Thm 1 proof, p004-b002]: if `P₁ ρ` and `P₂ ρ` five-cycle recognize
+`A₁` and `A₂` with output `ρ` for every five-cycle `ρ`, then `commutatorProgram P₁ P₂ σ`
+recognizes `A₁ ∩ A₂` with output `σ`.  On `A₁ ∩ A₂` the yield is `τ₂⁻¹ τ₁⁻¹ τ₂ τ₁ =
+θ (sigma2⁻¹ sigma1⁻¹ sigma2 sigma1) θ⁻¹ = σ` (`isFiveCycle_commutator`, `conjugator_conj`); off it
+two of the four blocks are the identity and the other two cancel.  A named step of C13's
+sketch.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Write `θ` for the conjugator and `τᵢ = θ * sigmaᵢ * θ⁻¹`, five-cycles by
+`Equiv.Perm.cycleType_conj`, as are their inverses.  By `yield_append` the yield is the product of
+the four blocks' yields, and each block's yield is `τ` or `1` according to its recognized set.
+Split on `A₁ x` and `A₂ x`: if both hold the product `τ₂⁻¹ τ₁⁻¹ τ₂ τ₁` equals
+`θ (sigma2⁻¹ sigma1⁻¹ sigma2 sigma1) θ⁻¹`, which is `σ` by `conjugator_conj` (group identities);
+otherwise the surviving blocks are `τ⁻¹` and `τ` for the same `τ`, or none, and cancel. -/
+private theorem commutatorProgram_recognizes {P₁ P₂ : Perm (Fin 5) → BranchingProgram 5 n}
+    {A₁ A₂ : (Fin n → Bool) → Prop}
+    (h₁ : ∀ ρ, IsFiveCycle ρ → FiveCycleRecognizes (P₁ ρ) A₁ ρ)
+    (h₂ : ∀ ρ, IsFiveCycle ρ → FiveCycleRecognizes (P₂ ρ) A₂ ρ)
+    {σ : Perm (Fin 5)} (hσ : IsFiveCycle σ) :
+    FiveCycleRecognizes (commutatorProgram P₁ P₂ σ) (fun x => A₁ x ∧ A₂ x) σ := by
+  classical
+  set θ := conjugator (sigma2⁻¹ * sigma1⁻¹ * sigma2 * sigma1) σ with hθ
+  have hc₁ : IsFiveCycle (θ * sigma1 * θ⁻¹) := isFiveCycle_conj isFiveCycle_sigma1 θ
+  have hc₂ : IsFiveCycle (θ * sigma2 * θ⁻¹) := isFiveCycle_conj isFiveCycle_sigma2 θ
+  have hθσ : θ * (sigma2⁻¹ * sigma1⁻¹ * sigma2 * sigma1) * θ⁻¹ = σ :=
+    conjugator_conj isFiveCycle_commutator hσ
+  -- the yield, as a product of the four blocks' permutations
+  have key : ∀ x, (commutatorProgram P₁ P₂ σ).yield x = ⇑(if A₁ x ∧ A₂ x then σ else 1) := by
+    intro x
+    rw [commutatorProgram_eq, ← hθ, yield_append, yield_append, yield_append,
+      (h₁ _ hc₁).yield_eq_ite x, (h₂ _ hc₂).yield_eq_ite x,
+      (h₁ _ (isFiveCycle_inv hc₁)).yield_eq_ite x, (h₂ _ (isFiveCycle_inv hc₂)).yield_eq_ite x,
+      ← Perm.coe_mul, ← Perm.coe_mul, ← Perm.coe_mul]
+    congr 1
+    -- off `A₁ ∩ A₂` the blocks cancel; on it the product is the conjugated commutator
+    by_cases ha₁ : A₁ x <;> by_cases ha₂ : A₂ x <;>
+      simp only [ha₁, ha₂, and_self, and_true, and_false, ↓reduceIte,
+        one_mul, mul_one, inv_mul_cancel]
+    rw [← hθσ]
+    group
+  rw [fiveCycleRecognizes_iff]
+  refine ⟨hσ, fun x => ⟨fun hA => ?_, fun hA => ?_⟩⟩
+  · rw [key, if_pos hA]
+  · rw [key, if_neg hA, Perm.coe_one]
+
+/-- A commutator program is nonempty when its first block is: `(∀ ρ, 0 < (P₁ ρ).length) →
+0 < (commutatorProgram P₁ P₂ σ).length` (`commutatorProgram_eq`, `length_append`).  Glue for
+C13 and C14. -/
+private theorem commutatorProgram_length_pos {P₁ P₂ : Perm (Fin 5) → BranchingProgram 5 n}
+    (h₁ : ∀ ρ, 0 < (P₁ ρ).length) (σ : Perm (Fin 5)) :
+    0 < (commutatorProgram P₁ P₂ σ).length := by
+  set θ := conjugator (sigma2⁻¹ * sigma1⁻¹ * sigma2 * sigma1) σ with hθ
+  rw [commutatorProgram_eq, ← hθ, length_append, length_append, length_append]
+  have := h₁ (θ * sigma1 * θ⁻¹)
+  omega
+
+/-- A commutator program of blocks of length at most `K` has length at most `4 · K`:
+`(∀ ρ, (P₁ ρ).length ≤ K) → (∀ ρ, (P₂ ρ).length ≤ K) → (commutatorProgram P₁ P₂ σ).length ≤ 4 * K`
+(`commutatorProgram_eq`, `length_append`) [Bar89, Thm 1 proof, p004-b002].  Glue for C14. -/
+private theorem length_commutatorProgram_le {P₁ P₂ : Perm (Fin 5) → BranchingProgram 5 n}
+    {K : ℕ} (h₁ : ∀ ρ, (P₁ ρ).length ≤ K) (h₂ : ∀ ρ, (P₂ ρ).length ≤ K) (σ : Perm (Fin 5)) :
+    (commutatorProgram P₁ P₂ σ).length ≤ 4 * K := by
+  set θ := conjugator (sigma2⁻¹ * sigma1⁻¹ * sigma2 * sigma1) σ with hθ
+  rw [commutatorProgram_eq, ← hθ, length_append, length_append, length_append]
+  have a := h₁ (θ * sigma1 * θ⁻¹)
+  have b := h₂ (θ * sigma2 * θ⁻¹)
+  have c := h₁ (θ * sigma1 * θ⁻¹)⁻¹
+  have d := h₂ (θ * sigma2 * θ⁻¹)⁻¹
+  omega
+
+/-- Every Barrington program is nonempty: `0 < (barrington c σ).length`.  The proof of C14's
+`barrington_length_pos`, placed before C13, which needs it for Lemma 2 in the `∨` case.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Induction on `c` (`TreeCircuit.ind`) generalizing `σ`, by the readers of
+`barrington`: literals and constants have one instruction; a fan-in-1 node is its child's
+program; the `∧` and `∨` programs contain the first child's program as a block
+(`commutatorProgram_length_pos`; `length_complementLast` for the `∨` case's complements). -/
+private theorem barrington_length_pos_aux [NeZero n] (c : TreeCircuit n) (σ : Perm (Fin 5)) :
+    0 < (barrington c σ).length := by
+  refine TreeCircuit.ind (motive := fun c => ∀ σ, 0 < (barrington c σ).length) ?_ ?_ c σ
+  · rintro ⟨i, s⟩ σ
+    cases s
+    · rw [barrington_lit_false, length_ofPerm]
+      exact Nat.one_pos
+    · rw [barrington_lit_true, length_ofPerm]
+      exact Nat.one_pos
+  · intro b cs ih σ
+    rcases cs with _ | ⟨c₁, _ | ⟨c₂, cs⟩⟩
+    · cases b
+      · rw [barrington_node_false_nil, length_ofPerm]
+        exact Nat.one_pos
+      · rw [barrington_node_true_nil, length_ofPerm]
+        exact Nat.one_pos
+    · rw [barrington_node_singleton]
+      exact ih c₁ (List.mem_singleton.2 rfl) σ
+    · have h₁ := ih c₁ (List.mem_cons.2 (Or.inl rfl))
+      cases b
+      · rw [barrington_node_false_cons_cons, length_complementLast]
+        exact commutatorProgram_length_pos
+          (P₁ := fun ρ => (barrington c₁ ρ⁻¹).complementLast ρ⁻¹)
+          (fun ρ => by simp only [length_complementLast]; exact h₁ ρ⁻¹) σ⁻¹
+      · rw [barrington_node_true_cons_cons]
+        exact commutatorProgram_length_pos (P₁ := fun ρ => barrington c₁ ρ) h₁ σ

+/-- The composition tree of an instruction list `l` computes the yield of the program `⟨l⟩`:
+`(compTree l i j).eval x = decide ((⟨l⟩ : BranchingProgram w n).yield x i = j)`.  Glue.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Well-founded recursion on `l.length`, following `compTree`.  Empty list:
+`compTree_nil`, `const_eq`/`const_eval` and `yield_nil`.  One instruction: `compTree_singleton`,
+`Instr.wire_eval`, and `yield_eq` with `List.foldl` on `[ι]`.  Otherwise (Step 1) `⟨l⟩` is
+`⟨l.take m⟩ ++ ⟨l.drop m⟩` (`append_instrs`, `List.take_append_drop`), so (Step 2)
+`compTree_cons_cons`, `yield_append` and `wireComp_eval` with the recursive calls close it. -/
+private theorem compTree_eval_list :
+    ∀ (l : List (Instr w n)) (x : Fin n → Bool) (i j : Fin w),
+      (compTree l i j).eval x = decide ((⟨l⟩ : BranchingProgram w n).yield x i = j)
+  | [], x, i, j => by
+    rw [compTree_nil, yield_nil, id_eq]
+    by_cases h : i = j
+    · rw [if_pos h, ← TreeCircuit.const_eq, TreeCircuit.const_eval]
+      exact (decide_eq_true h).symm
+    · rw [if_neg h, ← TreeCircuit.const_eq, TreeCircuit.const_eval]
+      exact (decide_eq_false h).symm
+  | [ι], x, i, j => by
+    have hy : (⟨[ι]⟩ : BranchingProgram w n).yield x = ι.eval x := by
+      simp only [yield_eq, List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_nil, Function.comp_id]
+    rw [compTree_singleton, Instr.wire_eval, hy]
+  | ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l, x, i, j => by
+    -- Step 1: the program is the concatenation of its two halves.
+    have hsplit : ∀ (m : ℕ) (l' : List (Instr w n)),
+        (⟨l'⟩ : BranchingProgram w n) = ⟨l'.take m⟩ ++ ⟨l'.drop m⟩ := by
+      intro m l'
+      have h : (⟨l'.take m⟩ ++ ⟨l'.drop m⟩ : BranchingProgram w n).instrs = l' := by
+        rw [append_instrs]
+        exact List.take_append_drop m l'
+      exact (congrArg BranchingProgram.mk h).symm
+    -- Step 2: compose the two halves.
+    rw [compTree_cons_cons, hsplit ((ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l).length / 2) (ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l), yield_append]
+    exact wireComp_eval
+      (fun x i j => compTree_eval_list ((ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l).take ((ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l).length / 2)) x i j)
+      (fun x i j => compTree_eval_list ((ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l).drop ((ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l).length / 2)) x i j)
+      i j x
+termination_by l => l.length
+decreasing_by
+  all_goals simp only [List.length_take, List.length_drop, List.length_cons]
+  all_goals omega

+/-- The composition tree of an instruction list `l` has depth logarithmic in `|l|`:
+`(compTree l i j).depth ≤ (Nat.clog 2 w + 2) * Nat.clog 2 l.length + 1`.  Glue.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Well-founded recursion on `l.length`, following `compTree`.  The leaves have
+depth `≤ 1` (`depth_const`, `Instr.depth_wire_le`).  For `L = |l| ≥ 2`: (Step 1)
+`⌈log₂ L⌉ = ⌈log₂ ⌈L/2⌉⌉ + 1` (`Nat.clog_of_two_le`); (Step 2) both halves have length
+`≤ ⌈L/2⌉` (`List.length_take`, `List.length_drop`), so by the recursive calls and
+`Nat.clog_mono_right` their wires have depth `≤ (⌈log₂ w⌉ + 2)·⌈log₂ ⌈L/2⌉⌉ + 1`; (Step 3)
+`depth_wireComp_le` adds `⌈log₂ w⌉ + 2`. -/
+private theorem depth_compTree_list_le :
+    ∀ (l : List (Instr w n)) (i j : Fin w),
+      (compTree l i j).depth ≤ (Nat.clog 2 w + 2) * Nat.clog 2 l.length + 1
+  | [], i, j => by
+    rw [compTree_nil]
+    split_ifs <;>
+      (rw [← TreeCircuit.const_eq, TreeCircuit.depth_const]; exact Nat.le_add_left 1 _)
+  | [ι], i, j => by
+    rw [compTree_singleton]
+    exact (Instr.depth_wire_le ι i j).trans (Nat.le_add_left 1 _)
+  | ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l, i, j => by
+    -- Step 1: `⌈log₂ L⌉ = ⌈log₂ ⌈L/2⌉⌉ + 1` for the length `L ≥ 2`.
+    have hlen : 2 ≤ (ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l).length := by
+      rw [List.length_cons, List.length_cons]
+      omega
+    have hc := Nat.clog_of_two_le (b := 2) (by norm_num) hlen
+    -- Step 2: both halves have length at most `⌈L/2⌉`, so the induction hypothesis bounds them.
+    have hT : ∀ i j, (compTree ((ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l).take ((ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l).length / 2)) i j).depth ≤
+        (Nat.clog 2 w + 2) * Nat.clog 2 (((ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l).length + 2 - 1) / 2) + 1 := by
+      intro i j
+      refine (depth_compTree_list_le _ i j).trans (Nat.add_le_add_right
+        (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.clog_mono_right 2 ?_)) 1)
+      rw [List.length_take]
+      omega
+    have hD : ∀ i j, (compTree ((ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l).drop ((ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l).length / 2)) i j).depth ≤
+        (Nat.clog 2 w + 2) * Nat.clog 2 (((ι₁ :: ι₂ :: l).length + 2 - 1) / 2) + 1 := by
+      intro i j
+      refine (depth_compTree_list_le _ i j).trans (Nat.add_le_add_right
+        (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.clog_mono_right 2 ?_)) 1)
+      rw [List.length_drop]
+      omega
+    -- Step 3: one composition circuit adds `⌈log₂ w⌉ + 2` levels.
+    rw [compTree_cons_cons]
+    refine (depth_wireComp_le hT hD i j).trans ?_
+    rw [hc, Nat.mul_add_one]
+    omega
+termination_by l => l.length
+decreasing_by
+  all_goals simp only [List.length_take, List.length_drop, List.length_cons]
+  all_goals omega

+theorem prefixVal_eq_of_false {f : ℕ → Bool} {i m : ℕ} (hle : i ≤ m)
+    (h : ∀ j, i ≤ j → f j = false) : prefixVal f m = prefixVal f i := by
+  induction m, hle using Nat.le_induction with

+  induction p with

+  | succ p ih => rw [prefixVal_succ, ih, Nat.mod_pow_succ, Nat.toNat_testBit, Nat.mul_comm]

+
+/-- Glue: over the depth run of `gs`, a gate has one level more than its deepest argument,
+measured by `vertexDepth`:
+`g.depth (runWith DAGGate.depth gs (List.replicate n 0)) =
+1 + (g.args.map (vertexDepth n gs)).foldr max 0`, by `DAGGate.depth_eq` and the reader
+`vertexDepth_eq` (`TreeDAG.lean`) on each argument. -/
+private theorem depth_runWith_eq {g : DAGGate} {gs : List DAGGate} :
+    g.depth (runWith DAGGate.depth gs (List.replicate n 0)) =
+      1 + (g.args.map (vertexDepth n gs)).foldr max 0 := by
+  rw [DAGGate.depth_eq, funext (vertexDepth_eq n gs)]
+
+/-- Glue: a one-gate gadget.  Emitting a single NAND gate `g₁` that reads the arguments of `g`
+and computes `g` meets `GadgetSpec` with depth factor `2`:
+`GadgetSpec n 2 (g.args.length + 2) DAGGate.IsNAND g gs (gs ++ [g₁], n + gs.length)`.  It
+covers the copied `¬` gate and `∨[] ↦ NAND[]`.
+
+**Proof sketch.** The new vertex is the last one, so its value and depth are `g₁`'s over the
+run of `gs` (`vertexValue_last`, `vertexDepth_last`); `depth_runWith_eq` gives one level over
+the deepest argument. -/
+private theorem gadgetSpec_single {g g₁ : DAGGate} {gs : List DAGGate} (hgs : GatesAcyclic n gs)
+    (hargs : ∀ a ∈ g.args, a < n + gs.length) (hg₁ : g₁.IsNAND) (hga : g₁.args = g.args)
+    (hval : ∀ vals, g₁.eval vals = g.eval vals) :
+    GadgetSpec n 2 (g.args.length + 2) DAGGate.IsNAND g gs (gs ++ [g₁], n + gs.length) := by
+  have hargs₁ : ∀ a ∈ g₁.args, a < n + gs.length := hga ▸ hargs
+  refine ⟨⟨[g₁], rfl⟩, hgs.snoc hargs₁, ?_, fun x => ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · simp only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton]; omega
+  · exact (vertexValue_last gs g₁ x).trans (hval _)
+  · simp only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton]; omega
+  · show vertexDepth n (gs ++ [g₁]) (n + gs.length) ≤ _
+    rw [vertexDepth_last, depth_runWith_eq, hga]
+    omega
+  · intro h hh
+    simp only [List.drop_left, List.mem_singleton] at hh
+    exact hh ▸ hg₁
+
+/-- Glue: a two-gate gadget.  Emitting a NAND gate `g₁` that reads the arguments of `g` and
+computes `¬g`, then its negation `NAND[g₁]`, meets `GadgetSpec` with depth factor `2`:
+`GadgetSpec n 2 (g.args.length + 2) DAGGate.IsNAND g gs

+and `∧[a, b]`.

+    (hval : ∀ vals, (!g₁.eval vals) = g.eval vals) :

+  have e : gs ++ [g₁, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩] = gs ++ [g₁] ++ [⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩] := by
+    rw [List.append_assoc]; rfl

+    rw [List.length_append, List.length_singleton]

+    (DAGGate.isNAND_iff _).mpr ⟨rfl, by simp⟩
+  refine ⟨⟨[g₁, ⟨.not, [n + gs.length]⟩], rfl⟩, ?_, ?_, fun x => ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/BranchingPrograms/Barrington.lean (Lean, at 597fb736e545706a058cc212243a13f6dadfeceb) =====

/-
